mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1.2M for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically worse than baseline (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which compresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede statistically significant underperformance (p > 0.12).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent increase in the RSAFS (personal savings rate) above 7% signals a liquidity trap, reducing the efficacy of monetary policy and resulting in muted S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: liquidity trap or zero lower bound environment
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from baseline during triggered episodes (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals robust demand expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered periods compared to baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month signals a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 0% AND PAYEMS < 0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered months compared to baseline (p > 0.20).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.7% for five consecutive months signals a manufacturing recovery, boosting earnings expectations and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered periods compared to baseline (p > 0.10).
